name: MariaDB
model: Tables of rows queried with SQL (a fork of MySQL, mostly wire and SQL compatible); JSON functions; VECTOR type since 11.7
engine_note: InnoDB by default (clustered B+tree, MVCC via undo logs); other pluggable engines such as Aria, MyRocks (LSM) and ColumnStore
consistency: Multi-row transactions (InnoDB). Default repeatable read; since 11.6.2 innodb_snapshot_isolation=ON rejects lost updates (closer to snapshot isolation); serializable optional. Replication async by default, so replica reads can be stale; Jepsen found Galera loses writes.

jepsen.version: MariaDB 10.0 with Galera Cluster (2015 blog post)
jepsen.finding: Galera claimed snapshot isolation but was designed without one of its key properties, so it allowed anomalies snapshot isolation forbids.
Galera lost committed transactions on crashes and partitions (even with flush on every commit), allowed lost updates in healthy clusters, and stale reads; four issues unresolved at publication.

scaling: Bigger machine; asynchronous or semi-sync read replicas; Galera multi-primary cluster; MaxScale proxy for routing; Spider engine for manual sharding.
version_note: 13.0 is a stable rolling (innovation) release; the newest long-term support series is 12.3 (12.3.3, 2026-08-24, supported to 2029-06-12).
reach: Reach for it when you want a fully open MySQL-compatible server (Linux distros ship it as the default MySQL), or need Galera multi-primary.
avoid: Avoid when you need exact MySQL 8+/9 feature parity (replication and JSON differ), or trust Galera to never lose acknowledged writes.
escape: A MySQL-family peer rather than an escape; chosen for a fully open MySQL fork or Galera.
chat: Same as MySQL: users, chats and messages, if your stack is MySQL-family.
notes: innodb_snapshot_isolation default ON from MariaDB 11.6.2 (read from the InnoDB system variables docs page on 2026-10-04). Series status from the downloads.mariadb.org REST API: 13.0 Stable/Rolling, 12.3 Stable/LTS. The 2015 aphyr.com post is UK-blocked; date read from the Wayback Machine copy and its finding summarised from the 2026 Jepsen report's recap. Server licence is GPLv2; MaxScale is under BSL (not the server).
